archetypes.name: dependency-gate
archetypes.rationale: The plan has a pervasive verify-first pattern gated on PR #3548 state; a reviewer should check whether each gate condition is precisely testable and whether the boundary between #3548-owned surfaces and net-new deltas is consistently drawn throughout the plan.
archetypes.prompt_body: For every verify-first clause in the plan, confirm the condition is unambiguous and mechanically testable at implement-time (e.g. reading a specific function or variable name from a specific file) rather than vague prose like 'may still' or 'could inline'. Check that the plan never instructs the implementer to patch surfaces that the hard-dependency PR #3548 is explicitly documented as owning (failure mode 1 in the plan). Confirm that each verify-first skip path (e.g. marker script absent post-#3548 → skip Item 4 entirely) names a concrete observable condition rather than a judgment call. Look for any cases where a verify-first gate controls both a code change and a doc/SECURITY.md change — if the code gate is skippable but the doc change is not, flag it as a gap. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: stale-anchor-invariant
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces paired input/output variable separation (_LOOP_SCOPE_ANCHOR_IN/_PARSED_SCOPE_ANCHOR_FILE, _RETALLY_SCOPE_ANCHOR_IN/_RETALLY_PARSED_SCOPE_ANCHOR_FILE) to prevent stale anchor leakage; verify this pattern is consistently specified for every handoff surface and that stale-seed test cases are called out for each one.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check whether the _IN / _PARSED variable-separation pattern is explicitly specified in the plan for every script that handles SCOPE_ANCHOR_FILE propagation: plan-review-loop.sh, run-step3-review.sh, SKILL.md re-tally block, and test-step3-orchestrator-fence.sh stale-seed pin. Confirm that for each surface the plan specifies unset-before-parse, stdout-KV-only persist (not input env), and stale-seed harness coverage. Identify any handoff script described in the plan where either the unset-before-parse step or the stale-seed test case is omitted. Verify that the terminal conditions permitted to write SCOPE_ANCHOR_FILE (ok, main-agent-vote-required) are listed consistently across the loop, relay, re-tally, and SECURITY.md subsections — flag any mismatch. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: security-claim-coverage
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds two-surface SECURITY.md coverage that distinguishes staged-anchor provenance from source-specific provenance for inline renderers; some inline content surfaces are verify-first gated, creating a risk that the doc overstates the actual trust boundary enforced by this change.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit each inline renderer surface the plan claims SECURITY.md will document (scope-anchor consumers, revise waterfall blocks, subprocess context bodies, assessor feature block legacy fallback) and check whether the plan's SECURITY.md language is conditional on verify-first gates or states unconditional coverage. For subprocess context bodies and revise waterfall blocks, the plan says content migration is verify-first — confirm the SECURITY.md section draft in the plan correctly qualifies coverage as post-verify or notes an open gap rather than asserting hardening. Check whether the assessor feature block provenance note (staged-anchor only when --feature-file is the staged anchor; otherwise source-specific) is consistently reflected in the render-assessor-prompt.sh and render-assessor-prompt.md plan steps. Confirm FINDING_8 (revise feature block provenance) is addressed in the SECURITY.md two-surface draft and not only in the approach section. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
